subChunks.title: Navigation Patterns — Tabs, Breadcrumbs, Pagination
subChunks.hookHtml: Navigation patterns — tabs, breadcrumbs, and pagination — are high-frequency components that appear in almost every content-heavy UI. Each has its own layout requirements, active state logic, and keyboard accessibility concerns. Mastering their Tailwind implementation means understanding active vs inactive state patterns, border-based indicators, and the role of aria attributes in communicating selection state.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Tab navigation

/* Tab bar — border-b creates the underline track */
<div class="flex border-b border-gray-200">
  <!-- Active tab -->
  <button class="px-4 py-2 text-sm font-medium text-blue-600
                 border-b-2 border-blue-600 -mb-px
                 focus-visible:outline-none"
          aria-selected="true" role="tab">
    Overview
  </button>

  <!-- Inactive tab -->
  <button class="px-4 py-2 text-sm font-medium text-gray-500
                 border-b-2 border-transparent -mb-px
                 hover:text-gray-700 hover:border-gray-300
                 focus-visible:outline-none transition-colors"
          aria-selected="false" role="tab">
    Stats
  </button>
</div>

Key pattern: -mb-px on tabs pulls the active tab's border-b-2 down to overlap the parent's border-b, creating a seamless active indicator.

Pill/segmented tabs

/* Pill-style tab bar */
<div class="inline-flex bg-gray-100 rounded-lg p-1 gap-1">
  <!-- Active -->
  <button class="px-4 py-1.5 text-sm font-medium text-gray-900
                 bg-white rounded-md shadow-sm">
    Week
  </button>
  <!-- Inactive -->
  <button class="px-4 py-1.5 text-sm font-medium text-gray-500
                 rounded-md hover:text-gray-700 transition-colors">
    Month
  </button>
</div>

Breadcrumb navigation

<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">
  <ol class="flex items-center gap-2 text-sm">
    <li><a href="/" class="text-gray-500 hover:text-gray-700 transition-colors">Home</a></li>
    <li class="text-gray-300">/</li>
    <li><a href="/quests" class="text-gray-500 hover:text-gray-700 transition-colors">Quests</a></li>
    <li class="text-gray-300">/</li>
    <li aria-current="page" class="text-gray-900 font-medium">Dragon Quest</li>
  </ol>
</nav>

Pagination

<nav aria-label="Pagination">
  <ul class="flex items-center gap-1">
    <!-- Prev -->
    <li>
      <button class="px-3 py-2 text-sm text-gray-500 hover:text-gray-700
                     hover:bg-gray-100 rounded-md transition-colors disabled:opacity-50">
        ← Prev
      </button>
    </li>

    <!-- Page numbers -->
    <li>
      <button class="w-9 h-9 text-sm font-medium text-white bg-blue-600 rounded-md">
        1
      </button>
    </li>
    <li>
      <button class="w-9 h-9 text-sm text-gray-700 hover:bg-gray-100 rounded-md transition-colors">
        2
      </button>
    </li>

    <!-- Next -->
    <li>
      <button class="px-3 py-2 text-sm text-gray-500 hover:text-gray-700
                     hover:bg-gray-100 rounded-md transition-colors">
        Next →
      </button>
    </li>
  </ul>
</nav>

Lyra: "Always add ARIA attributes to navigation patterns. Tabs need role="tab" and aria-selected. Breadcrumbs need aria-label="Breadcrumb" on the nav and aria-current="page" on the active crumb. Pagination needs aria-label="Pagination" on the nav and aria-current="page" on the active page button."

storyBeats.speaker: Lyra the Scribe
storyBeats.text: Navigation communicates location. A tab without an active indicator is a hallway with no signs. A breadcrumb without aria-current='page' is invisible to screen readers. Build navigation that communicates to every user — sighted, keyboard, and assisted.

storyBeats.speaker: The underline tab pattern (-mb-px trick)

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Build a tab navigation, breadcrumb, and pagination component:

  • .tab-bar: flex, border-b, border-gray-200
  • .tab-active: px-4, py-2, text-sm, font-medium, text-blue-600, border-b-2, border-blue-600, -mb-px
  • .tab-inactive: px-4, py-2, text-sm, font-medium, text-gray-500, border-b-2, border-transparent, -mb-px, hover:text-gray-700, hover:border-gray-300, transition-colors
  • .breadcrumb: flex, items-center, gap-2, text-sm
  • .page-btn-active: w-9, h-9, text-sm, font-medium, text-white, bg-blue-600, rounded-md
  • .page-btn: w-9, h-9, text-sm, text-gray-700, hover:bg-gray-100, rounded-md, transition-colors

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Build a complete profile navigation section from scratch: a pill-style tab selector (Overview, Quests, Achievements), a full breadcrumb trail with at least three levels, and a pagination control with prev/next buttons and 5 numbered page buttons (first one active). Add all appropriate ARIA attributes. No starter code.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the -mb-px trick in the underline tab pattern — what does it do, and what would happen without it? Walk through the ARIA attributes needed for tabs (role, aria-selected) and breadcrumbs (aria-label, aria-current). Why does pagination need aria-current='page' on the active button?

questions.prompt: An underline tab bar uses border-b on the parent and border-b-2 on each tab. The active tab's blue border-b-2 doesn't align perfectly with the parent's border-b. Which class on the tab buttons fixes this?
options: -mb-px — shifts the tab down by 1px to overlap and cover the parent's border
mt-px — shifts the tab up to align the borders
border-overlap — built-in Tailwind border alignment utility
questions.answer: -mb-px — shifts the tab down by 1px to overlap and cover the parent's border
questions.explanation: -mb-px applies margin-bottom: -1px, pulling the tab's bottom edge down by 1px. This makes the active tab's border-b-2 overlap and visually replace the parent container's border-b (1px), creating a seamless active underline indicator that appears to come from the same track.

questions.prompt: In a breadcrumb, which ARIA attribute should be applied to the current page's breadcrumb item?
questions.explanation: aria-current='page' tells screen readers that this element represents the current page in a set of navigation links. It's the correct ARIA attribute for the active item in a breadcrumb trail. For tabs, use aria-selected='true' instead — different patterns use different ARIA attributes.

questions.prompt: You need to display the active tab state using only CSS classes — no JavaScript class toggling. The active tab is tracked via an aria-selected='true' attribute. Which Tailwind variant applies styles when this attribute is present?
questions.explanation: Tailwind provides aria-{attribute}: variants that apply when the element has the corresponding aria-* attribute set to 'true'. aria-selected:text-blue-600 activates when aria-selected='true' is present on the element. This lets you drive active state from ARIA attributes without adding/removing CSS classes via JavaScript.
